design.affected_system: public digital services, identity, applications, appointments, and assisted access
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on end-to-end public-service journey friction
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for end-to-end public-service journey friction
pair privacy-preserving event, application, appointment, and contact journey diagnosis with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Page events, applications, errors, appointments, contacts, decisions, and outcomes remain distinct.
No automated score determines eligibility, enforcement, or denial without lawful human review.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for end-to-end public-service journey friction.

constraints.description: The digital public access and administrative service delivery diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: chief digital officer and administrative service delivery director
design.decision_question: Where do users encounter verified error, abandonment, repeat contact, language, access, or handoff friction?
design.family_title: Digital public access and administrative service delivery

independence_key.binding_constraint: The digital public access and administrative service delivery diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for end-to-end public-service journey friction passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: privacy-preserving event, application, appointment, and contact journey diagnosis
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible service journeys with unresolved verified friction

design.intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting end-to-end public-service journey friction, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible service journeys with unresolved verified friction
distributional gap in eligible service journeys with unresolved verified friction
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not interpret non-completion as ineligibility, user error, disinterest, or lack of need.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for end-to-end public-service journey friction passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

design.title: Diagnose digital and assisted-service journey friction
transportability_risks: Eligibility, identity, language, disability access, connectivity, trust, and service design differ.
Digital telemetry omits non-users and can encode device or tracking coverage.

family.affected_system: public digital services, identity, applications, appointments, and assisted access
claim_boundary: Service requests measure reported workload, not verified incidents, need, harm, or resolution.
Assignments and schedules are proposed operations, not completed work or public outcomes.
Design records do not establish agency adoption, deployment, productivity, or resident impact.
family.decision_owner: chief digital officer and administrative service delivery director
family.description: Eight decisions for journey diagnosis, channel forecasting, service redesign, assisted-access siting, support allocation, appointment scheduling, outage stress, and digital-service evaluation.
family.title: Digital public access and administrative service delivery

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
